TS7S2A.intro: Carry-forwards for TS7S2A (ts-node -> tsx and related), exact wording

carryForwards.wording: ts-node is the only in-tree consumer whose transpile follows the root tsconfig target (npx ts-node --showConfig now reports target es2017, module esnext, moduleResolution bundler, paths without baseUrl). Before replacing npx ts-node in the four terminology:* scripts with tsx, run npm run terminology:validate once with ts-node and once with tsx and diff stdout; record both exit codes and the diff in the local receipt.
carryForwards.concern: terminology:validate with ts-node and with tsx, stdout diff and both exit codes

carryForwards.wording: scripts/tsconfig.json still carries baseUrl ../src and paths {"@/*": ["./*"]}; TypeScript 7.0.2 rejects it with TS5102. No in-tree runner references it (tsx resolves the root tsconfig from cwd). Leave it to TS7S2OD (OD-scripts-tsconfig); if kept, the D2 form is paths {"@/*": ["../src/*"]} with baseUrl deleted. Do not let TS7S2A touch it.
carryForwards.concern: scripts/tsconfig.json keeps baseUrl for TS7S2OD; TS7S2A must not touch it
carryForwards.applies: TS7S2A (must not touch) and TS7S2OD (task 2.5, OD-scripts-tsconfig)

carryForwards.wording: The 13 ts-jest TS151002 messages in desktop npm test are informational (ts-jest forces CommonJS + Node10 for non-ESM runs). They disappear with task 2.3 (ts-jest -> @swc/jest). Until that unit lands, do not add diagnostics.ignoreCodes to desktop/jest.config.js; after it lands, assert in the 2.3 receipt that the message count is 0.
carryForwards.concern: 13 informational ts-jest TS151002 messages until task 2.3; no diagnostics.ignoreCodes; 0 asserted in the 2.3 receipt
carryForwards.applies: TS7S2A (desktop npm test proof) and TS7S2B (task 2.3)

carryForwards.wording: An emit-equality receipt that builds into out-of-tree sibling directories must say that each .map's sources entry embeds the checkout directory name relative to the outDir, so per-file .map hashes are reproducible only from the same path. When base and head are different checkouts, build into each tree's own dist (sources become ../../...) so a reviewer can match .map hashes too.
carryForwards.concern: out-of-tree emit builds embed the checkout name in .map sources

carryForwards.wording: The Next build emit is produced by SWC with env.targets from browserslist and reads no tsconfig target (next/dist/build/swc/options.js); the C6 whole-project emit manifest when root typescript becomes the TS 6 alias is still worth producing once for tsc itself, but a Next output comparison is not needed for a compiler-version change.
carryForwards.concern: no Next output comparison needed for a compiler-version change; a tsc whole-project emit manifest is still worth producing once

carryForwards.wording: Desktop nodenext emit identity rests on desktop/package.json having no "type": "module"; any unit that adds it must redo the 1.4 byte-for-byte proof, because nodenext would then emit ESM.
carryForwards.concern: desktop nodenext emit identity rests on no "type": "module" in desktop/package.json

M2 (documentary): removing baseUrl also removes <root>/src from Next's webpack resolve.modules (explicit-baseUrl-only behaviour). 0 bare src-subdirectory imports exist, so no effect; design.md D2 does not mention this resolver side effect. No edit requested now.

M4 (toolchain): 13 informational TS151002 messages in desktop jest; harmless; removed by task 2.3. See C3.

resolverSideEffect.wording: One real resolver change: webpack-config.js pushes the baseUrl onto resolve.modules only when it is explicit ("Only add the baseUrl if it's explicitly set"), so bare imports rooted at a src subdirectory (e.g. 'utils/logger') would no longer resolve in webpack. My scan of 8,291 ts/tsx/js files under src, e2e, scripts, .storybook, server.js, next.config.ts, playwright.config.ts, desktop/electron, desktop/services and openspec/scripts found 0 such imports (and tsc under the old baseUrl was the only thing that ever accepted them), so no effect (M2).
resolverSideEffect.summary: Next webpack drops <root>/src from resolve.modules when baseUrl is implicit; 0 bare src-subdirectory imports rely on it, so there is no effect today.

tsJestMessages.wording: npm run electron:test (desktop jest): base 5 suites / 57 tests, 0 TS151002; head 5 suites / 57 tests, 13 TS151002 messages. ts-jest 29.4.6 source (legacy/compiler/ts-compiler.js): fixupCompilerOptionsForModuleKind forces module CommonJS and moduleResolution Node10 for every non-ESM run regardless of the tsconfig module, and the TS151002 message is raised purely because the initial module kind is Node16/NodeNext. Informational; acceptable until task 2.3 replaces ts-jest (M4).
tsJestMessages.authorConcern: ts-jest TS151002 (13 informational messages): acceptable until task 2.3; the compile is forced to CommonJS/Node10 anyway (section 4). Suppressing via diagnostics.ignoreCodes would need desktop/jest.config.js, which is not a leaf; do not add it here.
